strategyPosture: Stay deployed in confirmed 1m leaders (META, VST, SPY) and let the DATA_AHEAD dislocations (BWXT, NOW, MDB) season — the pullback screen says research-screened, verify thesis before sizing any position, and there is no reason to add risk two weeks ahead of the 10/14 CPI binary.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real, but credit says this is rotation, not a rollover: bank lending standards are loose (SLOOS 0% vs ~40% stress threshold), HY OAS is tight at 3.02, and VIX is 16.12. No credit confirmation of broad stress, so weakness concentrated in former leaders stays a leadership problem, not an index problem.
themes.dataAnchor: Beneath the surface, the Mag7 averages 12.97% off their 52-week highs — an 11.07-point divergence gap vs SPY. TSLA is 29.3% off its high (weakest of the group); NVDA at -3.9% is the strongest. Two holdings — NFLX (-14.53% 1m) and UBER (-11.89% 1m) — sit on the 1m laggard list while QQQ is +2.83% 1m. IWM is -5.83% 1m and -7.11% 3m: small caps are not participating.
themes.label: Index leadership rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: SPY sits only 1.9% off its 52-week high, so the surface read is a calm market grinding higher.
themes.watchFor: If SLOOS lifts off 0% toward the ~40% stress line, or HY OAS widens materially from 3.02, the rotation read breaks and rollover risk takes over.

themes.counterRead: Price says the trade is over; the P&L says the businesses are accelerating. That is the setup the watchlist promotion (BWXT score 70, cyclical trough, demand inflection structural) is flagging. Risk: LEU's -70.2% drawdown shows not every nuclear name is a sentiment victim — distinguish operators with revenue from stories with leases.
themes.dataAnchor: BWXT is 42.9% below its 52-week high with RSI 33.4 (near oversold) while revenue grows 26.1% YoY with $185M positive FCF and a tier-B conviction score of 77. CCJ holds a tier-C score of 64 with RSI 34.7. The demand theme is not dead — it is political now: 'AI industry moves to thwart data centre backlash ahead of US midterms' is an active anticipated event signal.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market has treated nuclear/AI-power as a spent momentum trade — URA -12.4% 1m, CCJ -12.8% 1m, SMR -16.25% 1m, and LEU 70.2% below its 52-week high.
themes.watchFor: BWXT RSI reclaiming 45+ on rising volume, or the watchlist promotion converting to a conviction tier, would confirm the trough; a break to RSI <30 is capitulation and a better entry, not a stop.

themes.counterRead: MDB's ACUTE_CATALYST tag is the honest warning — a 24.5% one-month drop on an event means the thesis needs the catalyst named before sizing. But across the cluster, durable-moat software is growing 20%+ while priced at cyclical-trough multiples. The market is charging a disruption discount on businesses still compounding.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue lines disagree with the derating: NOW revenue +23.1% YoY, MDB +22.8% YoY with 71.8% gross margin and $500M FCF (20.3% margin). Both carry watchlist scores of 72 and 69 with 'recovery confirmed' revenue inflections, and MDB holds tier-B conviction (77). HUBS's -60.7% drawdown is tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental.
themes.label: Enterprise software washout: priced for disruption, growing through it
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is being derated as an AI-disruption casualty — NOW 32.7% off its high (RSI 45.4), MDB 28.7% off (RSI 37.7, flagged ACUTE_CATALYST), HUBS 60.7% off (RSI 36.5).
themes.watchFor: MDB identifying and clearing its acute catalyst; NOW or MDB watchlist-to-conviction promotion; HUBS RSI breaking below 30 for the final washout entry.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and price agree that crypto beta is leading, so no divergence to fade. The structure matters though: beta-over-spot outperformance is leverage-chasing inside the bid — the first thing to crack if the 10/14 CPI print reprices risk. This is a ride-with-a-seatbelt position, not a thesis to press.
themes.dataAnchor: The leadership is real in price — five crypto-linked names in the top 12 one-month performers. But the bid is concentrated in leveraged proxies: BMNR (+13.28%) and CONL (+8.47%) are outrunning spot BTC-USD (+7.14%) by 1.3 to 6.1 points.
themes.label: Crypto beta leads the 1m tape
themes.narrative: Risk appetite is back in the highest-beta wrappers: BMNR +13.28% 1m, ETH-USD +9.24%, IBIT +8.13%, COIN +7.8%, BTC-USD +7.14%, CONL +8.47% all sit in the 1m leader list, and the BMNR holding is riding it.
themes.watchFor: Spot BTC-USD reclaiming leadership over BMNR/CONL would signal a healthier bid; the reverse — proxies fading while spot holds — is the early exit tell.

themes.counterRead: VIX 16.12 prices no fear into a known binary — the 'on edge' narrative and the complacent vol print cannot both be right. A hot CPI on 10/14 into a quiet Fed reprices the 10/27-28 path fast, and the pain lands first on the -29.3%-from-highs Mag7 tail (TSLA) and IWM (-7.11% 3m).
themes.dataAnchor: The data matches a market waiting, not a market stressed: DGS10 5.26% with a +0.34 2s10s curve (positively sloped, no inversion), real 10y at 2.91%, breakeven inflation 2.35%, HY OAS tight at 3.02, VIX 16.12. The 9/16 FOMC is past; the next decision is 10/27-28, after the CPI print. IAU is a holding and META (+26.68% 1m, +2.32% today) leads — duration and mega-cap growth are both being bought into the wait.
themes.label: Rates firm, credit calm, CPI on deck
themes.narrative: Headlines say the market is 'on edge' ahead of inflation data, with 7 news hits on the 10/14 September CPI print and a new Fed chairman who 'has a lot less to say than his predecessor.'
themes.watchFor: CPI Sep print on 10/14 vs consensus; any single-day VIX spike above 20 before the print; DGS2/DGS10 repricing of more than 25bp in the week after.

watchFor: CPI September print on 10/14 vs consensus — reprices the 10/27-28 FOMC path
SLOOS lending standards lifting off 0% toward the ~40% stress threshold — flips rotation to rollover
HY OAS widening materially from 3.02 — credit confirmation of stress
Mag7/SPY divergence gap closing toward 0 or stretching past -15 pts — leadership resolution either way
BWXT/NOW/MDB watchlist-to-conviction promotions, or RSI <30 capitulation on BWXT (33.4 now) as the entry trigger
whereWaveBuilds: The next real move builds around the 10/14 CPI print into the 10/27-28 FOMC: with VIX at 16.12 pricing calm and headlines already 'on edge,' a hot print hits the Mag7 tail and small caps first, while a cool print is the all-clear for the DATA_AHEAD software and nuclear names to re-rate on their revenue numbers.
